stops.note: a tavern-keeper or petty trader, the kind of Roman merchant Germanic peoples met along the frontier
turned into a verb 'to trade', the source of German kaufen 'to buy'
a market or bargain, surviving in London's Cheapside and towns like Chipping Norton
shortened from 'good cheap', a good bargain, to mean low-priced

current_meaning: low in price; of poor quality
